mechanism: Everything right of the periodic left nursery is one structure: 1-runs of length 1, 2 or 3 separated by gaps of length 0 or 3 mod 4 (L_gap). Read by gap residue, the units are 0/1 counter digits (0000/1000), pass blocks P = 11000, walls W0 = 0 11000.. and W1 = 1 11000.., and shifted digits S1 = 0 1000. One B arrival is an exact carry rewrite: 0->1 stop, 1->0 go on, P passes, S1->P stop, SP (W0)->W (W1) stop, W -> three carries to its right, then P plus a shift that attaches to the next run. The conveyor walls, the binary counter and wall absorption are all this one rule. The blank run stays in L_gap to 2e10. L_gap is not closed in general: it is left only when a W1 wall whose wire is down to one block finishes a round while the digits above it wrap to exactly 0 under a wall-type unit, which leaves a shift directly on a wall (0111000). That is a counter-value coincidence.
closed_gaps: Right barrier = binary counter, digits 1000/0000 on a period-4 lattice, one increment per B arrival; rule K: (10111)^m B> (1000)^j 0 --> <C (11000)^m (0000)^j 1 in 5m+8j+1 steps (192/192, random m,j>=0); a wire block 11000 inside the zone passes carries through

Complete rule coverage from the blank tape to 20,000,003,117 steps: 6 sweep macros (SR, SR6, SL', SL, KB, KC; variable n) + 13 fixed junction rewrites (J1-J5 at walls and zone, J6-J10 at the left edge, J11-J13 in the first 75 steps); macro sim matches the C core exactly at 1e8, 1e9 and 2e10; each junction holds with random outside context (520/520)

Wall rotor law made exact: the event order at each wall is fixed by its state (b b c c c); W1 pass forwards exactly 3 arrivals, W0 forwards 0; a binary digit is the same kind of rotor with 2 in, 1 out

Interior wires never shrink: leftward crossings alternate +0/+1 block (right wall's W0 bounce, then its Lw3 pass), and the left wall eats 1 block per 3 crossings, so the length at successive W1 passes goes +0, +1, ... (derived lemma; consistent with 160/160 random-wire closure runs)

This one language covers the walls, wires, counter digits, P blocks and the single-0 shifts that round 1 could not place

Single-0 shifts explained: a shift is the cell of a W0 wall whose wire has run out (S1 = 0 1000 or SP = 0 11000). It travels up through 0 digits, turns into P at the next 1 digit and into a wall at the next P. Offsets 1 and 2 halt because they are two shifts in one gap (gap 1 or 2 mod 4), which L_gap excludes

Wall absorption is the W rule: the last wall's final round (wire = 1 block) leaves P plus a shift that attaches to the first run above. On a 1 digit it becomes S1, which later becomes P. On a zone P it becomes a zone wall (SP) that climbs through P blocks and dissolves at the next 1 digit

round2_remaining_gaps: Coincidence condition (the one open point): L_gap is left only if a W with a 1-block wire finishes a round while the k digits between it and the next non-digit unit X wrap to exactly 0 (value 2^k-3 before its 3 carries, k>=2) and X is a wall (SP or W). To 2e9 there is never more than 1 zone wall, and no two wall units are separated by digits alone (zonewalls2.py). Still, 6 of 11 zone-wall records have only digits below the zone wall. Excluding the coincidence needs either a timing argument (a zone wall over k digits moves on after 2^(k+1) carries, but the next last wall arrives only after about 3x its wire length in carries) or a larger closed language that contains the shift-on-wall states

Leaving L_gap is not immediately fatal: 154 forced coincidences in coinc.py all ran 3000 arrivals without halting, but a looser language that allows 4-runs degrades and can halt (explore5.py: 1 halt, 38 bad exits in 3000). So the shift-on-wall states need their own rules before a closed superset of L_gap can be stated
